case.description: The case's ID in the declared case list.

RunAbortParams.description: What `run.abort` takes: the Run, and whether the abort was forwarded.

forwarded.description:
Set by an engine that forwards the abort to the owner the Run index
names (ADR 0031): an engine that does not own the Run then answers
`run_not_owned` instead of taking its writer role.

RunAxes.description:
A Run's three axes as they are now (ADR 0029): what
`run.axes_changed` reports, and what a resync gives of each Run.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope, once it ended.

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed, once it ended.

location.description:
Where to write the Checkpoint, a path on the engine's machine; by
default where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, its own folder.

run_epoch.description: The run epoch the Checkpoint is taken under.

blocked.description: Also the requests whose latest outcome is `blocked`.

RunId.description: A Run ID (ADR 0036): lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.

RunIndexRow.description:
One row of the Run index (ADR 0031): a Run, where its state is, its three
axes and, while it is live, the engine that owns it.

kind.description: What kind of Run it is.

location.description:
Its folder: relative to the per-major data folder when it is inside,
absolute otherwise.

owner.description:
While it is live, where the engine that owns it is reached: a
Daemon's endpoint, or an Attached engine's private endpoint. An
engine that cannot take the Run's writer lock forwards live actions
there.

presence.description: Whether its state is at its location.

RunKind.description:
What kind of Run it is: a Collie Run its program drives, or a crawl
(ADR 0102), which its start's inputs name.

oneOf.description: A Run its program drives page by page.
A crawl, whose work items the engine leases to its handlers.

RunOrigin.description: Where a run-layer value came from (ADR 0083).

oneOf.description: A call's argument.
A scope's `settings` option.
A CLI flag.
An Integration's form.

after.description:
Where to start: after this position, or `now` for the next commit
on; absent, from the first outcome.

kinds.description: Only outcomes of these kinds; absent, every kind.

labels.description: Only outcomes of requests of these Labels; absent, every Label.

RunOwner.description: Where the engine that owns a live Run is reached (ADR 0031).

oneOf.description:
A Daemon, at the endpoint of its runtime file, which also holds its
token.
An Attached engine, at its private endpoint.

RunReport.description:
What a Run states about itself when it ends (ADR 0102): its three axes
(ADR 0029) and when it ran.

checkpoint.description:
The last Checkpoint written of it in this engine, when one was (ADR
0102).

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope.

policy_version.description:
The version of the Operator policy it ran under, when one applied
(ADR 0028).

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed.

weakened_by.description:
Every setting it ran with that weakens a guarantee class or switches
off a costly control, with its value and layer (ADR 0028).

checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint to resume from, a path on the engine's machine, which
becomes the Run's state in this engine's run folder; by default the
Run resumes from its run file on this machine.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

settings.description:
The Run's settings from the resume on, nested by key: the run layer
(ADRs 0083 and 0102).

seeds.description:
Each seed's answer, in the order the start gave the seeds; none for
a Run that is no crawl.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

run_id.description:
The Run's ID; the engine generates a lowercase ULID when it is
absent. An existing ID returns that Run when the caller and the
inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

RunStarted.description: What a start answers once its Run is started, never at its end.

needs.description:
The Product it needs (ADR 0098): Collie until it uses an entry the
catalog marks Foxhound's, Foxhound from then on.

RunStateRow.description: One row of a Run's run state about itself: its `run` table (ADR 0002).

binding.description: What the Run is bound to (ADR 0056), as JSON, or none.

clean_up_digest.description:
The digest of the Clean-up rules the Run holds to, which a resume
keeps (ADR 0047), or none.

inputs.description: Its start's inputs, as canonical JSON, which a later start compares.

journal_position.description:
How many commits the run file holds: the position of its journal,
which a Checkpoint reports (ADR 0002).

kind.description: What kind of Run it is.

policy_version.description: The version of the Operator policy it ran under (ADR 0028).

weakened_by.description:
The settings it ran with that weaken a guarantee or switch off a
costly control, as a JSON list of each one's key, value and layer
(ADR 0028).

RunsReindexOutput.description:
What `runs reindex --json` prints: the Run index it rebuilt, and how many
of its rows are of each presence.

erased.description: Rows of Runs discarded on purpose, kept erased.

missing.description: Rows it kept whose state it did not find.

present.description: Rows of Runs whose state it found.

echo.description: The text each page repeats, a type Collie's catalog defines.

SamplePageFilterAdmitParams.description: What a sample page filter is asked about a page.

SamplePageFilterAdmitResult.description: What a sample page filter answers about a page.

admitted.description: Whether the sample crawl visits the page.

key.description: The key to keep the value under.

SampleStorePutResult.description: What a sample store answers once it kept a value.

replaced.description: Whether a value was already kept under the key.

Seed.description:
One request a crawl starts from (ADR 0093): a URL, the Label that picks
its handler and its Payload.

payload.description: The data the program attaches for its handler.

priority.description:
Its priority among the requests of its domain: higher goes first,
and a priority never orders requests of different domains (ADR
0004); 0 by default.

Seeds.description: A crawl's seeds, at least one.

ServiceManager.description: The OS's service manager a Daemon is installed with (ADR 0024).

oneOf.description: macOS's launchd, as a launch agent with socket activation.
Linux's systemd, as a user unit with socket activation.
Windows' Task Scheduler, as a logon task.

SessionId.description: A Session of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

SettingLimit.description:
A setting that decided an outcome: its key, its value and the layer that
set it (ADRs 0028 and 0079).

SettingsExplanation.description:
What `config.explain` answers and `config explain --json` prints:
every setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer
that locked it (ADR 0028), and the files read.

files.description: The files of the configuration layers, lowest first.

policy_version.description:
The Operator policy's version, `sha256:` and the first 16 hex digits
of its file's digest, which the run report names; `None` without a
policy.

SettingsFile.description: A layer's file, as `config explain` names it.

found.description: Whether it exists; a missing file sets nothing.

SettingsLayer.description: The layers settings resolve through, lowest first (ADRs 0028 and 0083).

oneOf.description: The built-in default.
An Operator policy.
User configuration.
Project configuration.
A Recipe.

The run: a program's settings, a call's argument, a CLI flag or an
Integration's form.

Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

SkipReason.description: Why a crawl request was skipped (ADRs 0079, 0093, 0107 and 0119).

oneOf.description: A redirect left the crawl's scope.

A redirect or a Hook's rewrite reached a host the domain policy
refuses.
A URL rule merged it with a request already admitted.
The site's robots.txt refuses it.
The site's Crawl-delay could not be kept.
An AI-use signal refuses the Run's Purpose.
A before-request Hook skipped it.
Its handler skipped it.
The Run's Model allowance was reached.
Its response's content type is not one its Label takes.

StartedAs.description: Whether a start began its Run or found it.

oneOf.description: The start began it.

Its Run ID named a Run started before with the same inputs, which is
returned as it is.

It was interrupted and goes on from its committed state, its run
file or a Checkpoint, at the next run epoch (ADRs 0002, 0003 and
0102).

Status.description: Whether a Journey is still run.

oneOf.description: Run on every surface it lists.

Kept under its ID, never run; its file names `replaced_by` and a
`reason`.

manual.description: Why the step needs a person; a variant records it as `manual`.

on.description:
The one surface the step runs on in every variant, when the goal
needs that surface.

text.description:
What the person does, in declarative words that survive a change of
implementation.

oneOf.description: It ran and held.
It ran and did not hold.
An earlier failure stopped the variant before it.
It needs a person; the owner test covers it.

text.description: The step's text in the Journey.

StopReason.description:
Why a Run stopped (ADR 0102); the other causes join with the tickets that
stop Runs for them.

oneOf.description:
Its program, a person or a Client aborted it, a Connection's close
included (ADR 0078).

It was paused: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed by its Run ID
(RT-11).

It was migrated: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed from its
Checkpoint on another machine (ADR 0002).

Its `timeout.run` passed, and it stopped at its next safe point,
resumable with a fresh clock (ADR 0080); no Error code of its own.
A Client, such as through `$/cancel`.

SubscriptionEnded.description:
What `events.subscribe` answers when its subscription ends without the
Client cancelling it: the engine stopped.

version.description: The version of its case list.

oneOf.description: The TypeScript SDK.
The Python SDK.
A Rust program, through a Product's crate.
The CLI, as a Client of its own Attached engine or of a Daemon.
The MCP server, as a Client of a Daemon.
The Console.

Goodfetch Cloud's gateway, or the Stub gateway, which a Collie engine
takes as given to word `not_in_product`'s `fix` (ADRs 0095, 0096).

A Browser host, which is never a Client and needs no Product
(ADR 0095).
A Script sandbox worker.

SurfacePackage.description: The package of a Journey variant's surface.

Tag.description: An opaque text a Run is tagged with (ADR 0036).

Tags.description: A Run's tags, in the order given.

Target.description:
What a suite ran against: an engine over the protocol, the Browser host,
a process Plugin, Goodfetch Cloud's engine or, for the self-test, the
Proving ground itself.

oneOf.description: The version it reports, for an engine its Product version.
The SHA-256 digest of its artifact, for a target with no version.

product.description: For an engine, the Product its `hello` reply reports (ADR 0095).

TargetArtifact.description: A published file built for one target.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of what `url` serves.

target.description: The Rust target triple it was built for.

TaskResult.description:
One named Proving ground task: the oracle's answer and the server-side
observations.

answer.description: The oracle's answer; none when the variant never submitted a result.

observations.description: What the Proving ground observed for the task.

Verdict.description: Whether a Run's own checks prove what it committed (ADR 0029).

oneOf.description:
Every check the Run relies on passed, none was switched off, and no
Effect is left uncertain.
A declared Success check failed.
Everything else: a person reviews it.

cap.description: The largest value a higher layer may give a count or a duration.

max_requests_per_minute.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.

max_unused_age.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

concurrency.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

idle_timeout.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

echo_repeats.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.

first_byte.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

handler.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

lock.description: The values it sets and locks: no higher layer changes them.

max_requests_per_minute.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.

Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

domains.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

domain_keys.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.

concurrency.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.

handler_failed.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

idle_timeout.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

report_guarantee_class.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

write_ids_and_epochs.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

offline.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.

extra.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.

resolve.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.

chain_rpc_endpoints.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

domains.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.

exchange_rates.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

max_price_per_page.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

durability.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened_by`.

layout.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.

location.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.

source.description: Where a Session's login comes from. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.

trusted_cas.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: certificate files or Secret references. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

domains.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

domain_keys.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.

concurrency.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.

handler_failed.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

idle_timeout.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

report_guarantee_class.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

write_ids_and_epochs.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

offline.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.

extra.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.

resolve.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.

chain_rpc_endpoints.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

domains.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.

exchange_rates.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

max_price_per_page.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

durability.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened_by`.

layout.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.

location.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.

echo_repeats.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.

by_reference.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

source.description: Where a Session's login comes from. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.

first_byte.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

handler.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.

trusted_cas.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: certificate files or Secret references. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run.

denied_domains.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.

domains.description: The domains whose Walls a run may read past by generic means. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

refetch_domains.description: The domains on which reading past a Wall may fetch a page again. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration, never by an answer.

signing.description: Every webhook Goodfetch sends is signed, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

version.description: The version of this format the file was written in.
